meta.title: Product Roadmap Consulting | B2B | CommView
meta.description: Product roadmap consulting for B2B scale-ups. Turn strategy and evidence into prioritised outcomes and initiatives that can survive changing information.
secondaryKeywords: how to build a product roadmap

h1: Make the roadmap explain the decision.
hero.sub: A useful roadmap shows where the product is trying to create an outcome and why that work deserves priority. It should guide decisions without pretending the team can predict every feature and date months in advance.

diagram.caption: ROADMAP LOGIC
diagram.sub: Strategy becomes choices before it becomes work.

sections.heading: Why Most Product Roadmaps Fail
sections.intro: The roadmap becomes dangerous when it hides the reasoning behind the work.

items.title: Feature list disguised as strategy
items.body: The document records what will be built but cannot explain which outcome those features are intended to change.

items.title: The loudest customer wins
items.body: Individual requests become commitments without enough evidence that the underlying problem matters across the target market.

items.title: Sales pressure becomes product priority
items.body: Near-term deal pressure can override product strategy when there is no explicit decision model for trade-offs.

items.title: Dates become promises
items.body: A planning view is treated as certainty even when discovery and delivery are still generating new information.

sections.targetKeyword: how to build a product roadmap
sections.heading: How to Build a Product Roadmap From Strategy, Not Requests
sections.intro: The roadmap should make the logic visible.

steps.title: Strategy
steps.body: Clarify the customer, problem and product direction.

steps.title: Outcomes
steps.body: Define the customer or business change the product needs to create.

steps.title: Bets
steps.body: Choose the product opportunities most likely to influence those outcomes.

steps.title: Prioritise
steps.body: Compare evidence, value, risk, dependencies and effort without pretending the scoring model makes the decision for you.

steps.title: Initiatives
steps.body: Translate priorities into coherent areas of work rather than premature feature commitments.

steps.title: Learn
steps.body: Use discovery and delivery evidence to update the roadmap as assumptions change.

sections.heading: One Product Roadmap Does Not Need to Say the Same Thing to Everyone
sections.intro: Different audiences need different levels of detail, but the underlying product logic should remain consistent.

columns.title: Sales and customers
items: No invented certainty about dates or features

items.q: How far ahead should a product roadmap look?
items.a: A product roadmap should look far enough ahead to communicate strategic direction without pretending distant work is certain. Near-term initiatives can carry more detail because evidence and delivery constraints are clearer. Further out, themes, outcomes or strategic bets are usually more honest. The appropriate horizon depends on the product, market and planning cadence.

items.q: Should the sales team see the full product roadmap?
items.a: Sales should understand product direction and the context needed for customer conversations, but that does not require exposing every internal planning detail as a commitment. A sales-facing view can communicate relevant themes and confidence levels while protecting the team from accidental promises. The underlying strategy should remain consistent across versions.

items.q: How do we prioritise between competing customer requests?
items.a: Start by separating the requested feature from the underlying customer problem. Compare how often and how severely the problem appears in the target market, its strategic fit, expected value, evidence, risk, dependencies and delivery cost. Prioritisation frameworks can organise the evidence, but product judgement still has to make the trade-off.

sections.heading: A roadmap should make trade-offs clearer, not hide them behind dates.
sections.body: Build a roadmap that connects strategy, evidence and delivery without turning uncertainty into false promises.
